problem: Set pay fairly without negotiation bias.
title: Buffer publishes its salary formula and every individual salary
context: Buffer was a small remote company that already valued transparency.
decision_made: Use a published formula based on role, seniority, experience and location, and share all salaries publicly.
action_taken: Published the formula in December 2013 and has kept transparent salaries for about a decade.
observed_outcome: A 2015 LinkedIn article reported that Buffer received many more applications and that candidates were pre-screened for valuing transparency; Buffer said it once got 1,500 applications in just over a week for a content role. No measured before-and-after data was found.
lessons: Pay transparency can act as a filter on who applies, though the effect is hard to quantify.
limitations: Evidence is company statements and an interview. The formula has changed since 2013. No measurement of the effect on retention or cost was found.

claims.claim_text: Buffer published a salary formula and its individual salaries.
A 2015 article said Buffer received many more job applications and that applicants were pre-screened for valuing transparency.
